content.text:
No, it isn't safe without a prefix. Unprefixed `--color-*` variables go on `:root` and can collide with variables on your users' sites.

The fix is the `prefix` option, which prefixes the generated CSS variables as well as the classes:
- `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` compiles to `--tw-color-red-500` (`src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts › Using the prefix option").
- You still write `@theme` variables without the prefix, such as `--color-avocado-100`. The output gets `--tw-color-avocado-100` "to avoid conflicts with any existing variables in your project" (`src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx`, "Changes from v3 › Using a prefix").
- You keep built-in utilities like `rounded-lg`. They become `tw:rounded-lg`, so your users' class names change too.

The docs don't say whether this prefixes only the variables you actually use. I didn't find anything on tree-shaking unused built-in variables, so I can't confirm that from these docs.

No, it isn't safe without a prefix. Unprefixed `--color-*` variables go on `:root` and can collide with variables on your users' sites.

The fix is the `prefix` option, which prefixes the generated CSS variables as well as the classes:
- `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` compiles to `--tw-color-red-500` (`src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts › Using the prefix option").
- You still write `@theme` variables without the prefix, such as `--color-avocado-100`. The output gets `--tw-color-avocado-100` "to avoid conflicts with any existing variables in your project" (`src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx`, "Changes from v3 › Using a prefix").
- You keep built-in utilities like `rounded-lg`. They become `tw:rounded-lg`, so your users' class names change too.

The docs don't say whether this prefixes only the variables you actually use. I didn't find anything on tree-shaking unused built-in variables, so I can't confirm that from these docs.
